title: Beyond the 956: Bonnie Tyler, voice of 'Total Eclipse of the Heart,' dies at 75
excerpt: Bonnie Tyler, the Welsh singer whose powerhouse voice carried “Total Eclipse of the Heart” to No. 1 around the world, died July 8, 2026, at 75 in Faro, Portugal. Her final recording, “Love, Light and Peace,” was released November 13.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Bonnie Tyler, the Welsh singer whose powerhouse voice carried “Total Eclipse of the Heart” to the top of the charts around the world, has died at 75.

Tyler died on July 8, 2026, in a hospital in Faro, Portugal, after an illness, her family announced the next day. “Bonnie unexpectedly passed away in hospital in Portugal as a result of the illness she was being treated for,” the family said in a statement posted on her official website.

Tyler had undergone emergency surgery in May for a perforated intestine and was placed in a medically induced coma. She never fully recovered.

Born Gaynor Hopkins on June 8, 1951, in Skewen, Wales, Tyler broke through with “It’s a Heartache” in 1978. Her defining hit came in 1983 with “Total Eclipse of the Heart,” written by Jim Steinman, which reached No. 1 in the United States and Britain and became one of the best-selling singles of the decade. A year later, “Holding Out for a Hero” became another signature song through the film Footloose. The Grammy-nominated singer kept recording and touring for more than four decades, and “Total Eclipse of the Heart” returned to the British singles chart after her death as fans revisited her catalog.

Tyler’s final studio recording, the Christmas single “Love, Light and Peace,” recorded in December 2025, was released on November 13, 2026. Her husband of 53 years, Robert Sullivan, said she would have wanted her fans to hear it.

Tyler was laid to rest in her hometown of Swansea, Wales, in August, where thousands of fans lined the streets to pay tribute.

Rest in Peace, Bonnie Tyler.

Sources: BBC (July 9, 2026); The Guardian obituary (July 9, 2026); Bonnie Tyler official website; Official Charts.
